scope: N3.1a native process authority, checked execution, ownership inspection and shutdown; OMP hosts, containment, supervision and N4-N7 incomplete
sourceManifestAlgorithm: SHA256 of sorted relative path + NUL + file SHA256 + newline

adaptations: Calls use a test-only CLI adapter to Rust; original process assertions are retained.
Python controls delayed/frozen fixture processes only; checked execution is Rust. The concurrent shared probe remains Python to verify lock interoperability.
Frozen dispatch holds a real inherited shared lock across SIGSTOP and exec, then invokes Rust epoch/lease validation.
Duplicate rejection accepts either a held lease or an already-written owner, while requiring one execution and unchanged winning logs.
nativeProcessEvidence.claims: Actual local processes, inherited locks, signals, bounded logs, disposable Git and controller death. No OMP, model, Mail, Docker, native workflow admission or live provider proof.

behaviorReferences.LIF-04/LIF-07: Real controller mutual exclusion, durable epoch rotation and retained Python/Rust lock interoperability. Independent OMP hosts remain N3.1b.
behaviorReferences.LIF-05: Only authenticated process groups receive termination; actual child progress stops, and the live parent receives exit code or signal correctly.
behaviorReferences.LIF-07/LIF-09: Stale/forged PID records and surviving escaped lease holders remain uncertain. Delayed helpers cannot cross controller takeover or an immutable seal.
behaviorReferences.REP-05/EVD-02: Disposable real Git reset restores a large tracked file and index. This validates checked execution, not N4 worktree admission or revision evidence.
behaviorReferences.SEC-02: Private immutable manifests/owner/logs, command/environment hash binding and server dispatch fence. Arbitrary command containment remains N3.2 Docker.
behaviorReferences.UI-03: Asynchronous process inspection yields; output capture remains bounded after controller death. Native UI/terminal proof remains N6.

developmentFailures.resolution: 18/19 scenarios passed. The final fixture stopped at workspace/workbench diagnostic wording before its timed takeover check. Align the retained workbench diagnostic; the full 25-scenario frozen run passes.
The installed TypeScript CLI requires --ignoreConfig when explicit files are given. Correct the standalone harness-check invocation; no source type error was reported.

auditCorrections: Preserve plain-host recursive directories and macOS path aliases; canonical paths remain mandatory for checked descriptors.
Checked preparation refuses a root created by a racing preparer instead of writing into it.
Failed seal preflight remains uncertain even when an earlier sealed receipt is stopped; covered after real controller-directory movement.
Controller lock probes distinguish contention from OS errors and retry interrupted flock calls.
limitations: The native service still uses exclusive dispatch and exposes no execution admission. Runtime shared-dispatch authority is confined to the new helper/library boundary until N3/N4 integration passes.
The 25 scenarios execute real disposable local processes and Git. Python is a fixture controller for SIGSTOP/delayed exec and interoperability only; the native helper does not invoke Python or Node.

The retained suite is adapted mechanically with exact source/adapted hashes. Its duplicate-launch diagnostic accepts either a held lease or an immutable existing owner; execution count and winning output remain strict.

A frozen fixture owns the real dispatch inode across SIGSTOP and exec, after which Rust performs its own epoch/lease validation. This is explicitly a fixture latch, not a hidden production environment switch.

Ownership uses the supported macOS ps/lsof interface and kernel flock. PID alone never authorizes signaling; escaped holders remain operator-held. This is not a sandbox or proof that arbitrary descendants are contained.

The checked helper retains at most 128 KiB per stream, drains both pipes after limits or log-write failure and keeps repository output unrestricted. capture.json records output retention only, not a crash-durable command exit result.
OMP RPC/host identity, provider model policy, Docker cleanup, external Mail, scheduler recovery and N4-N7 remain required. No real model/Jira/Bitbucket delivery or retained pilot state was touched.
All 27 frozen checks passed without retry; the two development failures remain recorded.
